rounds.proof_sketch: When count_include_pad=True (default/configured value), line 57 sets count=kernel_size. Since kernel_size≥1 (always positive), count>0 is always true. The difference between 'count>0' and 'count>=0' only manifests when count==0, which is unreachable with this configuration.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the guard condition from 'count > 0' to 'count >= 0'. The only behavioral difference occurs when count equals exactly 0. However, the model is configured with count_include_pad=True, which forces count to equal kernel_size (line 57). Since kernel_size is always a positive integer (at least 1), count can never be 0 under this configuration. Both predicates evaluate identically for all positive values of count, making this mutation semantically equivalent under the fixed configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant requires a configuration change (count_include_pad=False with padding>0) to expose the behavioral difference. Under the fixed configuration with count_include_pad=True, no value-level test can distinguish the mutant because count is always positive.
rounds.recommendations: For relational operator mutations on guard conditions, mutation testing tools should analyze whether the boundary value (here, count==0) is reachable under the fixed configuration. When the boundary is configuration-gated (as with count_include_pad), the mutation should be marked as configuration-equivalent rather than surviving tests.
